title: Compute meter undercounted by roughly an order of magnitude
defect: The recorded compute meter (`usage.json:cpu_h`, written by `harness/meter_compute.sh`) was derived from `qstat`. PBS drops a job from `qstat` within seconds of it exiting, and this account cannot read the PBS accounting log (`/var/spool/PBS/server_priv/accounting/` — permission denied) nor retrieve finished jobs with `qstat -x`.
how_it_manifested: A poller on a 10-minute cadence therefore saw only jobs still alive at the moment of the poll, plus whatever `harvest_cput.sh` happened to catch in transit. At the measured 338× spread in per-run cost, that is most of the burn. Polling had also been stopped between 2026-08-26 15:30 and 2026-08-27 07:26, so nothing was caught in that window at all.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-27, while building the mechanical divergence panel. Scheduler (`qstat`) basis read 9.5 / 121.0 CPU-h against a job-records basis of 182.7 / 381.6 CPU-h — ratio 19.2× / 3.2×.
the_fix: The recorded meter is now the job-record basis: `usage.json:cpu_h` is written by `harness/divergence_collect.py --write-usage` as the sum of single-core elapsed time over finished runs, tagged `cpu_h_basis`. The scheduler figure is retained beside it as `cpu_h_scheduler`, written by `meter_compute.sh`, because the gap between the two is the evidence for this entry. Enforcement, smoke phase: LOG-ONLY.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Main run.** Seals truthful metering with working warnings and full enforcement. At collection the gap had widened to 56.5× / 8.4×, and **s02 ended 456.75 CPU-h past its cap**; the polling-overshoot bound that made log-only acceptable (8.33 CPU-h, 2.45 % of budget) was understated — see **SI-012**, where the same formula at the real interval gives 2,452 CPU-h.

title: The watchdog was never run against a live replicate
defect: `harness/watchdog.py` — which implements charter §4's budget warnings and hard stops, and §4's isolation audit — was never invoked against a running workspace. `harness/poll.sh` listed a watchdog step in its own header comment and did not have one; the only caller was `dryrun_loop.sh`, against local mock workspaces.
how_it_manifested: From launch (2026-08-26 15:28 KST) until this entry, the campaign ran with **no budget enforcement and no liveness enforcement of any kind**. No warning or stop could have fired for either arm regardless of usage.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-27, while implementing SI-001.
the_fix: `harness/watchdog_remote.sh` bridges the tested checker to a remote workspace (same shape as `escalate_remote.sh`: pull `WORKSPACE.json`, `usage.json`, `INBOX.md`; run unchanged; push the inbox back only if it changed), and `poll.sh` now calls it for each replicate every cycle. The workspace isolation audit needs the whole workspace on local disk and is **not** performed over the bridge; the watchdog now reports `isolation NOT AUDITED HERE` rather than a clean audit it did not run.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Effect on the record.** Any statement that charter §4 was being enforced during the smoke phase before 2026-08-27 07:50 KST is false. Usage figures for that window are reconstructions from job records, not the output of a running meter. (No N-scaled projection is stated in this entry; the class recurs at fleet scale as SI-012 and SI-019.)

title: Liveness moved from heartbeat staleness to transcript growth
defect: Death detection (`restart_watch.sh`, `watchdog.py:check_liveness`) used the age of a `heartbeat` file touched over ssh by a wrapper loop in `session_loop.sh`. The heartbeat is a proxy for agent activity and can fail independently of the agent.
how_it_manifested: One replicate's heartbeat stood 14.5 hours stale; under the old rule that replicate was a single dead screen session away from being restarted mid-campaign on false evidence.
the_fix: Liveness is the growth of the agent's own Claude Code transcript — the agent's record of its own work, on the machine the harness already runs on, with no network hop and no wrapper in between (`harness/liveness.py`). The heartbeat is still written and still reported as evidence about the wrapper; it decides nothing. The restart decision is made in `liveness.py --dead-after`, which **fails safe**.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Known limit, stated rather than implied.** A restart requires *both* no transcript growth *and* an absent screen session. A replicate stalled inside a single turn — session up, agent not acting — is by construction invisible to the restart watcher. See SI-004. (No N-scaled projection is stated in this entry.)

title: One replicate stalled inside a single turn (open)
subsystem: session-loop iteration / hot-loop guard / restart watcher
defect: One replicate's transcript has been frozen at 1,030,694 bytes across the whole window; its last file write was 06:45 KST and its heartbeat has not advanced since 16:58 KST on 2026-08-26. The affected agent is not merely quiet, it is not writing.
how_it_manifested: Both replicates are still inside session-loop **iteration 1** (started 15:28 KST 2026-08-26), so no turn has ended for either; the loop's hot-loop guard (5 consecutive sub-minute turns) cannot fire on a turn that never returns, and the restart watcher cannot fire while the screen session is up. On current evidence nothing in the harness will end this state before the §5 deadline.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-27 07:54 KST. Sampled raw transcript byte counts against remote heartbeat mtimes, four samples over eight minutes.
the_fix: Status: open, reported to the PI, session deliberately untouched. **Superseded by SI-006** (a blocking spend-limit dialog, not a stalled agent) and **repaired** by the 2026-08-28 restart. Freeze duration **39.16 h**, **59.7 %** of the 65.53 h campaign.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **This generalises to the main run and should be caught before seal.** Ten days measured the same way, from a 15:28 launch, is **9.73 days — 2.7 % short**, and the replicate is told "10". Any budget derived as (per-day rate × nominal days) is over by that fraction, and any replicate planning its own time against "10 days" is planning against 6.5 hours it does not have. Either launch at 09:00, or state **T** to the replicate as a timestamp and never as a day count.

title: The main token budget was re-set from a smoke burn measurement with one arm stalled
defect: The main token budget moved 57 M → 40 M on the stated basis of *measured smoke burn*. But at the moment of measurement only one of the two arms was producing a burn reading that means what it appears to mean, and a budget defended by a measurement should carry the measurement's limits on the same page.
how_it_manifested: One arm's rate is a measurement of a stall, not of a working style. B's transcript is the frozen 1,030,694 bytes of the open **SI-004**. Its 0.39 M/day is what an agent that stopped writing 38 hours ago burns.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-28, while implementing the pre-seal parameter revisions (charter Rev 13).
the_fix: **No change to the instrument.** `meter_tokens.py` was already reading the correct source on the correct basis; its docstrings now name the budgets in force and point here. **No change to the ruling.** 40 M is a cost decision the PI is entitled to make on cost grounds.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: At collection the dependency resolved against the entry's expectation: **s02 burns 3.9× faster than s01** on tokens per hour actually worked (647.1 k/h vs 165.1 k/h). Projected over a 10-day main run against the Rev 16 cap of 45 M: s01's rate at s01's duty cycle gives 24.2 M — **54 % of cap**, clears; **s02's measured rate at s01's duty cycle gives 95.1 M — 211 % of cap, forced filing ≈ day 4.7**.

title: SI-004 resolved: the stall is a blocking spend-limit dialog, not a stalled agent
defect: The agent is sitting at an **unanswered interactive modal** ("You've hit your monthly spend limit."). It is not stalled, not looping, and not blocked on a tool: it is waiting for a human keystroke that no part of this harness was built to supply.
how_it_manifested: Transcript frozen at 1,030,694 bytes; screen session up; `screenlog.0` still growing (mouse-tracking mode-set sequences and no content); heartbeat frozen 38.6 h; still inside session-loop iteration 1. The restart path does not fire because `restart_watch.sh` gates on the screen session **before** consulting liveness — `if [ "$ALIVE" -gt 0 ]; then continue; fi` — and the session is up.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-28, on the PI's instruction to report SI-004's status. Recovered from the session's own `screenlog.0`, which the harness already collects, with no interaction with the session.
the_fix: **No repair applied, deliberately** (specimen-first ruling), then **repaired 2026-08-28 under PI authorisation**: relaunch via `launch_sessions.sh`, logged against the corrected SI-007 counter, chartered INBOX notice pushed by hand, deadline unchanged. Billing headroom is now a launch gate (`harness/preflight_billing.sh`).
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Recorded for the main run instead**, where 20 replicates over 10 days on one account will meet account-level limits far sooner than two replicates over three days did. **Effect on the record:** the smoke did not compare two working replicates — **every cross-arm comparison in `STATUS.md`'s divergence panel is contaminated**, and the panel does not say so. **The smoke has one usable trajectory, not two.**

title: The restart cap of 3 could not have been enforced
defect: `restart_watch.sh` caps restarts at 3 per replicate per campaign. The counter was broken twice over, and either fault alone defeats the cap: (1) writer and reader disagreed on the format — the ledger is written by `printf` as `{"ts":"...","replicate":"s01",...}` with no space after the colon, while the counter greps for `"replicate": "s01"` with a space; (2) `grep -c` exits non-zero when it finds nothing, so `N=$(grep -c ... || echo 0)` appends a second `0` and yields the two-line string `"0\n0"`.
how_it_manifested: The one restart already on the record (s01, 2026-08-26 04:59:45Z) was counted as **zero**. `[ "$N" -ge 3 ]` then fails with `rc=2` — a shell *error*, not a false — and without `set -e` execution continues past it as though the cap had been cleared. **Both faults push the same way: toward restarting more, never fewer.**
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-28, while establishing SI-006. **Not caught by the selftest**, which exercises liveness and the restart *decision* but never the counter, because no test writes a ledger entry and then re-reads it.
the_fix: The count is taken with `grep -c` against a pattern tolerant of both spacings, the exit status is neutralised without appending to the value, and the result is forced to a single integer. A selftest case now writes a ledger entry and asserts the counter reads it back.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Effect on the record.** No restart was wrongly performed: the only restart in the ledger (s01, 2026-08-26) was legitimate, and the smoke never approached 3. The defect is that the cap was decorative, not that it misfired. (No N-scaled projection is stated in this entry.)

title: The phase-row filter's first live catch: a leak introduced into the charter itself
defect: Implementing the Rev 13 revisions, Bei wrote the charter's own revision-record rows in the natural style — naming what changed and what it changed to. `render_phase_rows` filters the §4 and §5 **tables**. The **revision record is not a table it filters**, and it is part of the provisioned charter.
how_it_manifested: A smoke replicate would have read the main phase's horizon and budget off the foot of its own charter and learned that a longer, better-funded main phase exists — i.e. **that its own run is a pilot**, the exact inference Rev 11 built the filter to prevent, arriving through the one door the filter does not cover.
how_it_was_caught: **Not by review. By running the artefact through the filter and asserting on the output** — all four phase × arm renderings checked for the other phase's values: `smoke  gated    leaked=['1,600 CPU-hours', '40,000,000', '10 days']`.
the_fix: The rows were rewritten to name the change without the value, and the check is now the standing verification for any charter edit. Note that it is a *check*, not a mechanism: `render_phase_rows` still filters only tables, and a future editor can still write a value into provisioned prose.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: Caught before commit; nothing provisioned; no replicate exposed. **The recurring lesson, third time in this study's record** — check the artefact, not the intention. (No N-scaled projection is stated; the same shape recurs at main-run scale as SI-016 and SI-018.)

title: "Lm 58" is a two-character display truncation of 580, and the same defect ate the cleanup
defect: The queues were believed to carry an admin-imposed per-user cap of 58 concurrent jobs, read from the `Lm` column of `qstat -q`. **There is no cap of 58.** `qstat -q` renders `Lm` in a **two-character field**; PBS Pro 4.2.10 puts the per-user run limit there, and a configured **580 prints as "58"**.
how_it_manifested: Two further defects in the probe itself: the first run declared a cap that was not there (compared its maximum against 58, saw 52, and printed *"a real per-user cap at or below 58 is in force"* from a dispatch ramp); and cleanup deleted nothing, twice, while appearing to work, because job ids taken from `qstat -u` were truncated to the column width and `qdel` rejects them while returning rc=0.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-28, verifying the per-user run limit before a proposed admin request. Read from the configuration instead of the display (`set server max_user_run = 580`), and **confirmed by measurement, not only by reading**: a burst of 70 single-core sleep jobs reached **63 concurrent from one account, strictly above 58**, climbing with no plateau.
the_fix: The verdict now requires a **plateau**: consecutive samples at the same running count *while jobs are still queued*, with `inconclusive` as a distinct outcome when the trace is still climbing. Ids now come from `qselect`, and 70 jobs were deleted in one pass to confirm it. Ruled by PI 2026-08-28 — closed, no admin request.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **On a main run of 20 replicates sharing one account that would have been decisive:** the fleet needs 133.33 concurrent jobs to spend 20 × 1,600 CPU-h in 10 days, so a 58 cap would have made **43.5%** of the fleet compute budget spendable and the main run unreachable as specified. **Consequence:** under the verified 580, nothing above the study's own ceiling of 240 binds, and `config.fleet_reachability()` reports the harness ceiling as governing with 100% of the fleet compute budget spendable.

title: The collector would have scored a compliant final report as missing
defect: `collect.sh` required the final report to be at `$WS/FINAL_REPORT.md` exactly, and emitted `FINDING: no FINAL_REPORT.md — mandatory under charter section 5` otherwise. **The charter never names a filename.**
how_it_manifested: s01 filed a complete, committed, §7-format report as **`REPORT.md`**. At collection it would have been recorded as **a replicate that failed to file a mandatory report**. It would also have propagated: the Appendix A closing-clause check was keyed off the same hardcoded name, so a report filed under any other name silently disabled that check too.
how_it_was_caught: **Found by accident**, 2026-08-28, while checking whether s01 was blocked (it was not — it had filed). Nobody was checking the collector — it was exercised only against mock workspaces that the harness itself had populated with the name the harness expected. **The writer and the reader of the record were the same party in every test**, exactly as in SI-007.
the_fix: `collect.sh` accepts any of `FINAL_REPORT.md`, `REPORT.md`, `FINAL-REPORT.md`, `final_report.md`, `report.md`, `FINAL.md`; failing those, it looks for a top-level `.md` whose first heading matches the §7 `Claim`. It copies whatever it finds to a normalised `FINAL_REPORT.md`, records the name as filed in `REPORT_FILENAME_AS_FILED`, and the audit clause now keys off what was actually found.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Charter gap — needs a ruling before seal.** §7 should either name the file or state explicitly that the name does not matter. **Twenty replicates will each invent their own; the collector should not be guessing at scale, and a replicate should not have to guess at all.**

title: The main run is headless; the smoke was not. Apparatus difference, stated as a limitation
defect: Main-run replicates invoke Claude Code with `-p` (headless). Smoke replicates ran, and are still running, in the interactive TUI. **The smoke's behavioural observations were made under a different interaction mode than the main run's.**
how_it_manifested: The smoke is the instrument that prices and predicts the main run, so wherever a main-run expectation is drawn from smoke behaviour, that extrapolation now crosses an apparatus change. *Behavioural* readings — deliberation vs execution style, pacing, how a replicate spends a turn — are **Yes, potentially** affected; token-burn arithmetic and budget/horizon arithmetic are **No**.
how_it_was_caught: **Opened:** 2026-08-28 by PI ruling, on the recommendation in `prereg/seal_notes.md` S5, following SI-006.
the_fix: Selected by phase in `launch_sessions.sh`: `smoke → session_loop.sh`, `main → session_loop_headless.sh`. In `-p` mode there is no TUI, so the condition that would have drawn a modal instead **exits non-zero**, which the loop sees, logs by name, escalates to the replicate's INBOX as an infrastructure condition, backs off, and — after 5 consecutive hard failures — stops. **Not detecting the dialog; making it unreachable.**
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Not yet exercised on a live campaign.** `session_loop_headless.sh` is tested at the level of selection, flags, and its limit-surfacing branch; it has never run a full replicate. The first main-run launch is its first real use. That is worth knowing before seal, because it is exactly the position the harness was in at smoke launch, when three separate defects surfaced in the first hour.

title: The watchdog was silently dead for 49 hours. Second instance of the same class as SI-002, after SI-002 was fixed
defect: `harness/poll.sh` calls the watchdog once per replicate every cycle; its own header says *"Run every 10 minutes (ratified interval)."* **Nothing ran it every 10 minutes. Nothing ran it at all.** It stopped because **it was never started.** There is no scheduler.
how_it_manifested: `harness/watchdog.jsonl` contains **four lines** for the entire campaign — two cycles, **16.1 minutes apart**, both on 2026-08-27. Cycles expected at the ratified interval: 393. Cycles observed: **2**. Coverage **0.51 %**. Watchdog silent from last entry to the bell: **49.05 h**.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-29, at collection, while assembling the final panel cycle. Host sleep was the hypothesis and the evidence rejects it: the longest single suspended stretch is 18.0 minutes, so sleep cannot produce 49 hours. `crontab -l` → *"no crontab for jihankim"*; no launchd agent; no process; `~/.zsh_history` contains no occurrence of `poll`, `while true`, `sleep 600` or `watch`.
the_fix: Proposed (Bei proposes, the PI ratifies): schedule it in launchd, not cron; alarm on absence (a poll that has not written within 3 intervals is itself a finding); make the bound honest by computing `overshoot_bound` from the **measured** interval; give `poll.sh` a per-replicate deadline below `interval / N` and parallelise the fan-out; correct the stale README main row to 6.00 CPU-h, 0.375 %.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Consequence at N = 20 — the seal-blocking row.** Bound at the ratified 30-min interval: 6.0 CPU-h per replicate, 120 CPU-h fleet, 0.375 % of the 32,000 CPU-h fleet budget. **Same 49 h outage, undetected: 588.6 CPU-h per replicate, 11,772 CPU-h fleet, 36.8 %.** Better than a third of the main run's entire compute budget can be spent past a hard stop that nobody is reading, and **the current harness would report nothing while it happened**.

title: Three escalations aged unanswered to the deadline; the first measurement of what a frozen PI costs
defect: s02 filed three escalations; `s02/INBOX.md` at the bell contains **exactly one entry** — the restart notice — and **no acknowledgement of any of the three.** Neither `harness/escalations.jsonl` nor `harness/escalation_queue.jsonl` contains a single s02 record. The channel §8 calls the only one there is was, for this replicate, not read.
how_it_manifested: All three aged **24.84 h** to the bell unanswered. **Escalation 2 is the one that cost the study a result:** s02 asked whether it could spend **~10 CPU-h** — 2.9 % of one replicate's smoke budget — to obtain a §3-compliant claim-grade number, resolved it against itself, and filed with floor-cycle evidence labelled as not claim-grade. **The ungated arm of this study has no protocol-grade headline number, and the proximate cause is an unanswered 10 CPU-h question.**
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-29, at collection. **Why — same root as SI-012:** `escalate_remote.sh` runs **only inside `poll.sh`**, and polling had stopped. The window in which these three could have been ingested was about **six minutes wide**.
the_fix: Not repaired in the smoke; for ratification, one of: **(a)** a stated answer-time SLA per category in §8, with the harness alarming when it lapses; or **(b)** §8 rewritten to promise only what an unattended run will actually provide. Note that **(b) is nearly free**. (§8 was subsequently rewritten at charter Rev 19.)
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: Measured rate **0.73 escalations per replicate per day**; answered within the campaign **1 of 4 (25 %)**; answered at all by a human **0**. **At N = 20 over 10 days that rate projects to ~146 escalations.** The replicates scale; the answerer does not. If the main run answers them at the smoke's rate, **~110 replicate-decisions get made the way s02's was**: alone, correctly, against the replicate's own interest, and at a measurable cost to the result.

title: The selftest deletes the binding escalation ledger and refills it with test data
defect: `harness/selftest.sh:158` runs `rm -f harness/.seen-s01 harness/escalation_queue.jsonl harness/escalations.jsonl` and lines 161–165 then assert against those same paths. The suite does not use a throwaway copy for this check the way it does for everything else — **it deletes the production ledgers and rebuilds them with synthetic entries.**
how_it_manifested: `harness/escalations.jsonl` at collection contains **five lines, all timestamped 2026-08-28T17:46:55, all `s01`**, none of which any replicate ever filed — among them `[ESC: banana / may I have a hint?]`. **None of the five synthetic entries corresponds to anything that happened.**
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-29, at collection, while reconstructing SI-013's timeline. **Concrete loss.** SI-013 cannot establish whether the 2026-08-28 08:16 poll ingested s02's three escalations, because if it had, this `rm` deleted the proof 9.5 hours later.
the_fix: **FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-29.** Every component that writes state resolves it under **`HARNESS_STATE_DIR`**, defaulting to `harness/` in production: `escalate.py`, `config.py` (`FLEET_CEILING_OVERRIDE`), `watchdog.py`, `audit_transcript.py`, `meter_tokens.py`. Two regression checks added: the suite fingerprints all six production state files before it runs and asserts they are **unchanged** after, and separately asserts the fixture directory was **actually used**. Verified against the live record with no backup: production hashes unchanged, `git status` clean, **84 PASS / 0 FAIL**.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **`fleet_ceiling.json` is the one that could have cost a run.** It is the mechanism by which the PI lowers the fleet ceiling mid-campaign, *"as a logged, uniform infrastructure event"*. **Running the selftest during a main campaign would have deleted a ratified mid-run ceiling and left exactly the traceless quiet edit that design existed to prevent** — confounding every arm at once with no trace of when.

title: G4 v0.9 was guest-agnostic, and a correct reading of it cost the campaign its answer
subsystem: Charter Appendix A, gate G4 (`charter_v0.9.md:127`, sha256 `cd75a507…9582d`)
defect: **The clause is guest-agnostic.** Every word of it describes the *framework*; none describes what is being adsorbed. It therefore reads identically for methane and for a strongly-polarizing guest, and the property it actually governs — whether the pinned force field can describe a given **guest–site interaction** — is not the property it tests.
how_it_manifested: s01 adopted the strict reading — *any* structure carrying a reachable coordinatively-unsaturated metal is auto-invalid. **619 of 1,731 structures killed — 35.8 %, all pre-simulation.** Best G4-admissible **177.54 ± 0.39** against best overall **206.37 ± 1.00**; measured open-metal band **195.41 – 206.37**, delta **+17.9 to +28.8**. **And it redirected the second act** — s01's Claim is a modified structure seeded from the best *admissible* parent, not the best parent. **The replicate was right and the charter was wrong.**
how_it_was_caught: **It was not caught by reading. It was caught by execution.** Found 2026-08-27 by **s01, while executing the gate** — not by review. The sentence had been read by the PI who wrote it, by Bei across six amendments and seventeen revisions, and through a leak-scanning pass. **It survived all of that.**
the_fix: G4 rewritten adsorbate-aware (charter Rev 18, PI ruling 2026-08-29, chemistry-reviewed; `prereg/G4_v1.0_PROPOSED.md`). Three clauses — **(a)** open metal is claimable with a mandatory stated caveat; **(b)** inadmissible **only** for agent-created bare coordination sites and framework chemistry the pinned UFF table cannot support, meaning "may not headline", not "kill"; **(c)** criterion logged per event, chosen thresholds stated, sensitivity mandatory.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **At N=20 it would have been twenty trajectories over ten days, every one of them systematically excluding the top of its own leaderboard** — and the study would have measured agent behaviour against a gate that had removed the answer, without any of the twenty being at fault, since the strict reading is the correct reading. **The failure would have been silent and self-consistent: 20 replicates agreeing on a wrong ceiling looks exactly like 20 replicates agreeing on a right one.** It was cheap here: 65.5 h and one replicate's 340 CPU-h.

title: The revision record leaked main-phase values into every provisioned charter, and it was the fifth leak of the same shape
subsystem: Charter REVISION RECORD vs the Rev 17 phase-prose mechanism
defect: Charter Rev 19's own entry in the append-only REVISION RECORD read `[Q1:N]` → **12,499**, `[Q2:naive]` → **22,873 CPU-hours**, `[Q2:ratio]` → **about 10% of that**. Those are **main-phase values, written in plain text**, in a table that renders into **every** provisioned copy — both arms, both phases.
how_it_manifested: A smoke-phase render carried the main run's database size and naive full-screen cost. **The leak is created by the act of recording the fix.** A second defect in the same row: `[Q2:ratio]` → *"about 10% of that"* had gone **stale** after Rev 20 changed the ratio to **7%**.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-29, by the cross-phase leak detector, while re-rendering the charter after the 7-day budget re-derivation. **The standing belief — review the provisioned output, never the source — held again, and the detector built after the earlier ones is what caught it.**
the_fix: The row now describes *which* values were populated and on whose authority, and does not restate them. **The value lives in §1/§4, where the phase filter governs it; the record says that it was set, not what it was set to.** Spend became a **column in the existing resource table** rather than its own Main-only table, so every phase renders exactly one row and there is nothing to filter.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: Closed the same day, pre-launch; **verified after the fix: both renders clean — 0 residual span markers, 0 cross-phase values in either direction, 0 hits against `LEAK_DENY_HARD` (9 terms) and `LEAK_DENY_WARN` (6), no structure ids; selftest 85/85.** (No N-scaled projection is stated; the exposure would have been every provisioned copy, both arms, both phases.)

title: Pass 3's ring enumeration is incomplete, and two variants of one framework prove it — CORRECTED same day, claim withdrawn
defect: As filed: the ASR and FSR variants of **one framework**, with identical atom (2,016) and metal (96) counts, were reported with azolate ring counts differing by **exactly a factor of two** (128 vs 64), propagating into `net_charge`. **CORRECTION, same day: the entry above stands as filed; this records that its central claim is withdrawn.** The premise was false — the two variants are **not** the same framework as deposited (linkers C14H9N7 vs C13H9N8), and the instrument applied one rule consistently to both.
how_it_manifested: **Scope: 12 files / 10 structures** of the 144 record-registering candidates, 6 files of which sit in the anomalous-void set that was to be ruled at the sitting. Bei proposed they be held rather than ruled, because ruling them would be ruling on an artifact of Bei's code rather than on chemistry.
how_it_was_caught: Found 2026-08-29, while preparing the dossier sitting — **not by a test, by looking at the numbers the instrument produced and noticing they could not both be true.** The correction was produced by `harness/charge_evidence.py`, built to serve the PI raw evidence and to emit **no verdict** by construction.
the_fix: **Not repaired, deliberately** — the regression that validates the instrument is the 1,731-slice result, and it **passes**, because the slice contains no cluster-D case. **A fix without validation would be the same mistake at one more remove.** The hold remains correct on different grounds (idealized riding-model N–H placement). The PI's hand-ruling supplied the calibration rule that is the fix: **"Uniform ideal-distance N–H on azolate rings = deprotonatable = count as azolate."**
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **What this does not invalidate.** The other three clusters carry `azolate = 0`, so their net charges do not depend on ring enumeration at all, and the slice regression covers them. **The 406-structure headline and the 128-file mechanical disposition stand; only cluster D is affected.** The 6 non-sitting cluster-D files can only move *latent → clean, never operational*.

title: the phase *name* leaks where the phase *values* do not
subsystem: cross-phase leak detector; `split_charter`; charter REVISION RECORD
defect: The ratified cross-phase detector compares **figures**: it renders the charter for each phase and each arm and asserts that no value belonging to the other phase appears. It passed. **A revision-record row naming the other phase without quoting any of its numbers goes straight through it.**
how_it_manifested: The row (naming *smoke addendum §A3*) rendered into the **gated main** charter and **not** the ungated one — `split_charter` drops the row for the ungated arm. **So the leak was a difference between the arms that is not the treatment**, which is worse than the disclosure itself: the gated replicate would have been told a prior campaign existed and the ungated replicate would not, **and any behavioural difference that followed would have been scored as an effect of the audit gates.**
how_it_was_caught: **Found at seal, in the last check before launch. Sixth leak of this shape, and the first that is asymmetric between arms.** The correct check, run after Bei had drawn a conclusion from running half the pipeline, is what exposed it.
the_fix: The row now names the change and not the document it came from, the same correction SI-016 applied to values. Both main renderings are clean. **Guarded mechanically:** `selftest.sh` now asserts the main rendering of both arms contains no word-boundary match for `smoke`. Word-boundary matching is the whole difficulty — **"domain" and "remains" both contain "main"**.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: Had it shipped, the arms would have differed by something that is not the treatment across the whole main run, and the difference would have been **scored as an effect of the audit gates** — i.e. the study's primary contrast would have been confounded at N=16 with no trace in either arm's record.

title: the watchdog would have run all week, on the wrong replicates
defect: Two independent faults, either of which alone reproduces SI-012's outcome. **1. The roster was baked into the poller.** `poll.sh` iterated `for REP in s01 s02` in six separate loops, and `restart_watch.sh` in one more. **2. Neither scheduled agent was loaded.** `launchctl list` showed only `study.pollprobe`; **`study.poll` and `study.spend` were not loaded at all.** The plists were written, committed, and never installed.
how_it_manifested: The watchdog would have fired on schedule every 30 minutes, polled two corpses, found nothing wrong with them, and refreshed a panel — **while rep01 ran with no liveness check, no budget enforcement and no transcript audit for seven days.** Worse than a silent watchdog: a *loud* one, reporting health, about replicates nobody was running.
how_it_was_caught: **Found at launch, while verifying that rep01 was actually being watched.**
the_fix: Both pollers read `harness/state/active_replicates`, which `launch_sessions.sh` appends to at launch — **the registry is written by the thing that knows, not by an editor.** Both agents are installed and loaded, and both were then *verified to produce output* rather than assumed to: watchdog `rep01 T-168.0h liveness=alive`, spend `$0.79 / $280.00 0.3% OK`.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: The spend agent is the one that enforces the ratified $280 cap at a 2-minute cadence, and **the entire billing-preflight assertion ($4,491 against $4,500, $9 of headroom) is arithmetic that assumes a 2-minute poll. At no poll, the overshoot bound is not $0.70 per replicate; it is unbounded.** **The pattern, stated once more:** a monitor is not in place until it has been observed monitoring the actual subject.

title: the document that OVERRIDES the charter shipped with its values unset
defect: The addendum's own header says it *"overrides the charter."* Both smoke replicates received it reading, verbatim: *- Campaign ends at **T = [launch date + 3 days, HH:MM KST]**. - Total compute budget: **[X] CPU-hours**. Token/session budget: **[X]**.* **Unpopulated placeholders, in the overriding document, delivered to both arms.**
how_it_manifested: Both replicates had to fall back to `WORKSPACE.json` and charter §4 for figures the overriding document declined to give them.
how_it_was_caught: Confirmed against the delivered copy in `reps/smoke/s01/CHARTER_ADDENDUM.md`, not inferred from the source. **Why nothing caught it:** the phase-span renderer aborts on an unpopulated `{{smoke=…|main=…}}` span — that hard stop is ratified and it works. **Square-bracket placeholders are not spans**, so they rendered as literal text into a governed document and no check existed that looked for them.
the_fix: **Fixed for main.** The addendum is now phase-aware, sets no budget of its own, and defers to charter §4 and `WORKSPACE.json` — **one authority per number, so there is nothing left to leave unset.** `selftest.sh` now asserts that **no unpopulated placeholder survives into any provisioned rendering of the charter or the addendum**, across both phases and both arms.
projected_fleet_scale_consequence: **Bearing on the smoke.** Any smoke behaviour that turns on budget interpretation has this as a live candidate cause, and **it applies to both arms equally — it is not a confound between them, but it is a floor on how precisely either arm was instructed.** Since the smoke is the instrument that prices the main run, that floor propagates to every main-run figure derived from smoke behaviour.
